TMax-15K.reason: A QEMU VM whose SSH is exposed on localhost:2222 with password password123; must get the tunnel through it working. Same environment, same handles.
Write the qemu-system launch line with -netdev user,hostfwd mapping host 2222 to guest 22, plus the ssh command into the guest. The core mechanic.
Configure and daemonize sshd on port 2222 with a custom config, generate host keys, set the auth policy, leave it running. The sshd half exactly.
Repair a script that launches QEMU VMs and sets up network port forwarding, including startup ordering and keeping the VM alive.
Build a VM operator over QEMU: disk provisioning, launching VMs, and connectivity diagnostics against the guest, all without root.
Generate the exact qemu-system-x86_64 invocation with -netdev user,id=net0,hostfwd=tcp::HOST-:GUEST and a virtio NIC. Teaches the flag syntax.
Parse and validate QEMU startup configurations, including hostfwd=tcp::25-:25 and -virtfs mounts; forces real fluency in QEMU's CLI grammar.
Boot a QEMU VM in the background from a script, wire a proxy to the service inside it, and ensure both processes stay running after the script exits.
Multi-stage setup ending in a hardened SSH access point that must be live when the grader connects; same leave-a-service-running-and-reachable contract.
Write a VM deployment script that brings up a local VM with its network ports mapped and monitors it; deploy-a-VM-and-reach-it end to end.

Define a VM that runs under QEMU from a declarative config, including virtualisation options and the user account. Guest-config-then-boot.
Create an account with a password, start the SSH service, then prove it is listening and accepting connections. The guest-side half of the TB task.
Build a NixOS VM image for QEMU with a user, passwordless sudo and automatic login; configuring guest credentials so the VM is usable on boot.
Put sshd on a non-default port, open it through the firewall and verify the active Port directive. Non-standard-SSH-port configuration.
Start the local SSH server and confirm real connectivity, then manage authorized_keys. Start-sshd-and-prove-you-can-log-in.
Start and enable sshd and read back its configured Port; sshd_config editing and service startup, without any VM involved.
Probe localhost ports including 22 with telnet and write a connectivity report; the verify-the-service-is-actually-reachable habit.
Import a VM image into a hypervisor and configure it (memory, NIC model, disk bus) per a spec; VM disk/network provisioning, not QEMU CLI.
Assemble a boot command with kernel, initrd and console=ttyS0,115200; serial-console boot parameters are how you talk to a headless QEMU guest.

Build a qcow2 overlay over a cloud image and boot the VM with seed data so it comes up configured; the boot-an-image-with-injected-config move.
Generate a NoCloud seed image and boot a cloud image locally with it; same problem of getting credentials into a guest you cannot type into.

Root account is locked with no password; set a real password so the account can be used. The exact blocker on an Alpine image with an empty root password.
Drive a telnet login service as root with no password and capture what comes back; scripting a raw console login non-interactively.
Import an image and start a VM from a JSON definition with specific networking; provision-and-boot-a-guest, different hypervisor tooling.
Run a guest command under the QEMU i386 system emulator and capture its output; QEMU system emulation with record/replay, no networking.
Run a command over SSH on a non-default port with a socket forwarded over the connection; SSH forwarding plumbing on an odd port.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: SSH key exchange (GEX) breaks during Transport.connect; debugging the handshake that must succeed for the grader's ssh -p 2222 to work.
Transport.connect with username/password then open_session and exec_command; the client side of exactly the login the TB task must enable.
HostKeys fails to parse a known_hosts file; host-key handling is the thing that most often blocks an automated SSH login to a fresh VM.
ProxyCommand send/recv mangles byte counts; SSH transport plumbed through an external process, like reaching a guest through a forwarded port.
PublicBlob construction for SSH public keys breaks; SSH key blob encoding, relevant to host and authorized keys but not to the VM.
SFTPClient.from_transport crashes before the channel opens; debugging session setup over an established SSH transport.
generate_key_bytes produces wrong key material, breaking encryption; SSH crypto internals, a layer below what the TB task configures.
Socket creation from an address configuration fails; binding a daemon to a host:port is the other half of making port 2222 answer.
parse_address no longer rejects malformed tcp://host:port strings; careful reasoning about listen-address syntax and its failure modes.
Server will not start unless every binding option is given explicitly; debugging why a daemon fails to come up and listen at all.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: load_ssh_private_key behaves inconsistently on password-protected keys; SSH credential handling, though nothing about servers or VMs.
load_ssh_private_key lacks the validation-skip flag its PEM sibling has; OpenSSH key-format parsing in the same library.
SSH/SFTP URL handling changed across versions and paths resolve differently; reasoning about ssh://user@host addressing.
run-instances rejects a valid flag when launching a VM; instance-launch parameter validation, virtualisation-adjacent but emulated.
Awaiting an ssh subprocess loses the result object; driving an external ssh command from code and reading back its output.
Host:port parsing breaks when the string carries a scheme prefix; the same address-parsing care hostfwd and ssh -p arguments demand.
Connection upgrade to a raw bidirectional stream (docker exec) stopped working; hijacking a socket to talk to a container console.
Reproduction needs two real interfaces and iptables rules; reasoning about which local address a connection actually binds and leaves from.
A long-lived daemon's disconnect handling loops on retry; debugging a background service that must stay up and connected.
Bug reproduced against a server container with a host port mapped in; port publishing appears only as scaffolding, not as the problem.

notes: This TB2.1 task is unusually well served: TMax has a dense cluster of QEMU tasks that use the identical handles (hostfwd, port 2222, password123), and TerminalWorld contributes genuine boot-an-image-and-enable-root-SSH tasks, so final_top10 mixes the two. The retrieval order was misleading at the top for TMax: rank 1 (task_007993, 4/4 retrievers) is a git-hook/GitOps pipeline with no VM at all, and several high-rrf entries are generic 'SSH honeypot / SSH hardening' incident-response tasks that share only the token SSH; the genuinely matching QEMU tasks sat at rank 3, 6, 9 and in rest_ids. Recursive-Task-Synthesis matches heavily on the word VM but its 540 hits are dominated by two families (oVirt hosted-engine upgrades and imex4vm OCI-to-KVM imports) plus qemu-user-mode AArch64 assembly exercises, which are a different QEMU entirely (binary emulation, not system emulation) and were rejected. SWE-Rebench has essentially nothing: nine documents mention SSH at all and none concerns running a server, so its entries top out at overall 2. SWE-Smith reduces to paramiko, which is the client side of the protocol, plus gunicorn/daphne for socket binding. Overlaps heavily with qemu-startup, which I ranked next.
